item.title: Why a Palo Alto native traded in her tech career to start a Korean-inspired yogurt brand
item.description: Diana Lee is a self-proclaimed yogurt freak. The Atherton resident and Gunn High School alum is so passionate about the gut-friendly, high-protein snack that she quit her tech job to start her own yogurt company – and she’s documenting the entire journey on social media. The post Why a Palo Alto native traded in her tech career to start a Korean-inspired yogurt brand appeared first on Palo Alto Online.

item.title: East Palo Alto revives, modifies parking permit program
item.description: Seeking to address longstanding community complaints about illegal parking, the East Palo Alto City Council approved on Tuesday the first iteration of a revived Residential Parking Permit program that may offer two free parking permits to each residence and community petition options for permit zones. The post East Palo Alto revives, modifies parking permit program appeared first on Palo Alto Online.

item.title: Palo Alto Museum opening further delayed by water damage
item.description: The Palo Alto Museum, which was set to open this month after decades of planning and years of fundraising, will remain inaccessible for the foreseeable future after recent rains further damaged the basement level of the historical downtown building that will house the institution, the museum’s chief executive president said Tuesday. The post Palo Alto Museum opening further delayed by water damage appeared first on Palo Alto Online.

item.title: Chinese tea chain plans Bay Area debut in downtown Palo Alto
item.description: A Chinese tea chain with more than 10,000 stores globally is making its Bay Area debut – in downtown Palo Alto. Auntea Jenny, specializing in fresh fruit teas and other tea-centric drinks, expects to open this summer along University Avenue. The post Chinese tea chain plans Bay Area debut in downtown Palo Alto appeared first on Palo Alto Online.

item.title: City Council terminates Mountain View’s license plate camera contract
item.description: The Mountain View City Council unanimously voted on Tuesday to terminate its license plate camera contract with Flock Safety, heeding the calls of dozens of impassioned residents who spoke at the meeting urging the city to cut ties with the surveillance technology company. The post City Council terminates Mountain View’s license plate camera contract appeared first on Palo Alto Online.

item.description: This story was originally published by CalMatters. Sign up for their newsletters. item.title: East Palo council considers term limits for members
item.description: The East Palo Alto City Council on Tuesday expressed interest in floating a ballot measure in June that would allow residents to impose term limits on council members. The post East Palo council considers term limits for members appeared first on Palo Alto Online.

item.title: Builder gets a big boost for San Antonio housing project
item.description: Things are looking up for Yorke Lee, a local developer whose proposed housing project on San Antonio Road keeps increasing in height, density and unit count — all with the city’s enthuiastic support.
